title: SDKS: Fault-tolerant surface and evolution plan for pagination, retries, and streaming
creator: Anita Shah
summary: Define a clear, implementable client surface and backward/forward compatibility guarantees for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs covering pagination semantics, retry behavior, streaming APIs, and client evolution rules. Deliver PRD, acceptance criteria, interop test matrix, and migration guidance so SDK teams can ship consistent behavior across languages without breaking existing customers.
background: Multiple SDK teams and customers have reported divergent behavior across language SDKs for long-running streaming responses, opaque cursor handling for pagination, and retries around transient errors. Current incidents: streaming reconnects cause duplicate events for Node SDK consumers, Go SDK cancels pagination contexts prematurely, and Python retry wrappers swallow idempotency tokens. We need a product-led specification to align implementation and to define compatibility/deprecation policies.
goals: Define a single behavioral contract that all three official SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) implement for pagination, retries, and streaming
Minimize breaking changes to existing customers and provide clear migration steps for any incompatible changes
Provide an interop test suite and perf/regression targets to validate implementations
Ship documentation and example code for common patterns (cursor-based pagination, resumable streaming, client-side backpressure)
out_of_scope: Changes to server-side runtime internals unrelated to public API semantics
Billing or pricing changes tied to retry policies
requirements: Pagination: Server returns opaque cursor tokens. Clients must expose synchronous iterator (Go), async iterator (Python/TS), and explicit page()-based helpers. Iterator must be resumable given any cursor string. SDKs must normalize cursor appearance (base64 opaque string) and never expose internal route IDs.

Idempotency & retries: Define canonical idempotency token header (X-Redwood-Idempotency). Clients should automatically set a token for non-GET mutating calls unless user-provided. Retryable status codes: 429, 502, 503, 504 and network timeouts. Default strategy: exponential backoff with full jitter, initial=100ms, max backoff=10s, max attempts=5. SDKs must allow override and per-call disable. Retry must be transparent for idempotent operations and optional for non-idempotent with explicit opt-in.

Streaming APIs: Support chunked HTTP streaming and SSE-style event framing. SDKs must provide both convenience callback readers and low-level byte stream access. Streaming must be resumable where server supports resume token; otherwise client must expose a clear on-halting-reconnect behavior (error out vs. emit partial). Provide first-class cancellation: async context managers (Python), AbortSignal (TS), context.Context (Go).

Backpressure & concurrency: Node and Python async iterators must honor consumer-paced consumption; SDK must not buffer unboundedly. Go SDK must offer io.Reader-like stream with configurable buffer size. Default max in-flight token buffering per stream = 64KB.

Compatibility policy: Minor releases (x.y.z where y unchanged) are guaranteed non-breaking. Any breaking change must be announced with deprecation header, 6 months dual-support, and migration guide. Server will continue to accept old streaming format for 6 months from announcement.

Diagnostics & observability: SDKs must emit structured SDK-level events (retry, backoff, stream-resume, pagination-resume) to the customer's telemetry hooks and include local counters for retries and dropped events in debug logs.

Tests & interop: Provide canonical interop harness tests (pagination resume, retry scenarios, streaming resume, cancellation, backpressure) runnable in CI for each SDK. Specify test cases and expected traces/logs.
acceptance_criteria: PRD reviewed and approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) and runtime PMs
Interop test matrix created covering 20+ scenarios and checklists for each SDK
SDKs implement public surface for pagination/streaming/retries with consistent behavior across languages (verified by interop CI)
Backward-compatibility policy documented and posted to developer.guides with migration examples
Performance: common pagination/streaming patterns show <=5% median latency regression vs current SDK baseline in synthetic benchmark
Docs: Developer guides, code samples, and upgrade notes published for release sdk-2025.11
Security: Idempotency header and retry behavior reviewed by Security and approved (security_review_required=true)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Existing customers rely on current SDK quirks. Mitigation: dual-support period, migration guide, and opt-out flags in SDKs
Risk: Streaming resume semantics cannot be implemented for legacy server endpoints. Mitigation: server-side feature flag and graceful degrade path where SDKs surface non-resumable errors clearly
Risk: Increased client complexity causing regressions. Mitigation: interop test harness, staged rollout, and feature flags to disable advanced behaviors
Risk: Performance regressions in high-throughput workloads. Mitigation: benchmark targets and runtime perf review with ENG serving/runtime team

notes: Design trade-off: prefer explicit idempotency token vs heuristics to avoid accidental duplicate side-effects
Streaming format: choose simple JSON-lines framing with optional resume token as first field for maximum cross-language ergonomics
Pagination: prefer opaque cursor (server-controlled) rather than page-n offsets to allow internal shard/topology changes
Work closely with Dedicated/Private teams for any networking assumptions (HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 behavior)
